subject: Visibility supply chain: SIEM integration & connector plan
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood-inference.com>
To: Claire Dawson <claire@farmacyhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood-inference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood-inference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood-inference.com>, security@sentinelops.com
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Visibility supply chain: SIEM integration & connector plan

Hi Claire —

Thanks again for the time today. As discussed, FarmacyHealth will be running Redwood Private in your VPC (hybrid on-prem + cloud-proxied control plane). To make sure your SOC and IR processes are covered, we need to align on the observability export strategy and how you want logs/traces routed to your SIEM.

Key requirements we captured (attached sample mapping and a one-pager):
- Audit logs: all admin actions, deployment events, model rollout changes — retention 12 months (HIPAA-ish baseline).
- Inference metadata logs: request/response headers, anonymized request ids, model_id, latency buckets — retention 90 days.
- Traces: OTLP span export covering inference path and control-plane handshake, sampled at 1% standard, 100% on errors.
- Integrity & encryption: TLS1.2+ mTLS for forwarders, FIPS-validated KMS for any key material if you require it.

Proposed ingestion options (we want to validate one with your ops/security team):
A) Customer-side forwarder inside your VPC -> Syslog/TCP-TLS (port 6514) to your on-prem SIEM or to SentinelOps collector. Minimal egress with static IP allowlist.
B) HEC-style HTTPS endpoint (Splunk HEC) pulled from a forwarder with mutual auth.
C) SFTP drop for log bundles (batch) for slower retention flows (not recommended for traces).

Questions we have for you:
1) Does your SOC prefer persistent streaming (HEC/Syslog) or periodic bundle upload?
2) Any port/egress constraints (no outbound internet, forced proxy, deep packet inspection)?
3) Certificate/PKI requirements for mTLS (do you provide CA-signed certs or should we provision a client cert)?

Attachments included: observability_requirements_v1.pdf, sample_log_mapping.csv

Next steps I propose:
- Claire: confirm preferred ingestion mode and any explicit network constraints by EOD Wed.
- Ben: once Claire confirms, run a port & NAT check and share connector runbook.
- Laura: draft an IAM policy template for the forwarder in the VPC.
- Stephanie: coordinate evidence we may need for your SOC (SOC 2 artifacts, logging proof-of-rotation).

Happy to hop on a short technical alignment call this week if that helps — suggest Thu 10:00 PT.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood-inference.com

Thanks Marissa — good summary. A few quick notes from our side: 
- Our SOC prefers persistent streaming if we can get it to work reliably (HEC or Syslog/TLS).
- Network constraints: our prod VPC does NOT allow direct internet egress; all outbound must go through a controlled NAT/proxy run by our network team.
- Certificates: we use an internal PKI and would prefer the forwarder present a cert signed by our CA. We can provide a signing request or pre-signed certs.

Attaching our SLA constraints doc that highlights retention and encryption expectations (farmacy_sla_constraints.docx).

I'll confirm whether the proxy supports raw TCP 6514 or only HTTPS egress — should know by tomorrow.

— Claire
Claire Dawson
Head of IT Security, FarmacyHealth

From: SentinelOps <security@sentinelops.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood-inference.com>, Claire Dawson <claire@farmacyhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood-inference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 08:30:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Visibility supply chain: SIEM integration & connector plan

Hi all — thanks for pulling this together. Short note on options & what we recommend for a private deployment behind a restrictive egress proxy: 

Recommended approach (low friction + secure):
1) Deploy our lightweight forwarder as a private instance in your VPC (ami/container) that accepts local log streams from Redwood's local agents. Forwarder then sends encrypted data to your on-prem SentinelOps cluster using Syslog over TLS (TCP 6514) OR HTTPS HEC endpoint (TLS 1.2+).
2) If outbound internet is blocked, configure an egress rule that allows the forwarder to reach a small set of SentinelOps egress IPs at 443 and 6514. We support proxying via CONNECT/HTTPS if your proxy supports it.
3) Traces: we recommend deploying an OTLP gateway beside the forwarder that can accept OTLP/GRPC and forward spans to your tracing backend. Sampling controls live on the forwarder configuration.

Network notes: be aware of NAT translation for source IP allowlisting. If you require static source IPs we can propose a NAT pair or a small NAT instance inside the VPC. Also, mTLS will require cert exchange — we can accept CA-signed client certs or issue certs from our managed CA (we can supply a CSR flow).

Attachment: sentinelops_connector_spec.yaml (includes sample config for syslog/tls and HEC).

We can do a short runbook: port check -> cert exchange -> smoke test (1 hour), then phased consumption for production traffic. Happy to join Thu call if scheduled.

Regards,
SentinelOps Integration Team
security@sentinelops.com
(attachment: sentinelops_connector_spec.yaml)

Thanks Claire & SentinelOps — appreciate the detailed options. Summary of action items and owners: 

- Claire / FarmacyNetwork: confirm proxy capabilities (raw TCP 6514 allowed or only HTTPS connect) by Wed EOD — Claire (owner).
- Ben Carter (Redwood): schedule port connectivity & NAT validation with FarmacyNetwork; run the sentinelops_connector_spec.yaml in staging and report networking gaps (target Thu morning).
- Laura Bennett (Redwood): draft the forwarder IAM policy and least-privilege runbook; include S3 drop perms only if batch SFTP is used.
- Stephanie Nguyen (Redwood): assemble SOC evidence packet we might need to share with Farmacy's auditors (log retention proof, rotation logs, key-management notes).
- SentinelOps: provide a short smoke-test checklist & a sample TLS cert exchange workflow (owner: SentinelOps).

Proposed timeline: port & cert check Thu -> staging smoke test Fri -> production cutover next Tue (pending no blockers).

If that looks good, I'll create a calendar invite for Thu 10:00 PT to walk through the smoke-test steps.

--
Marissa Cole
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
